title: Prominent Israeli rabbi rules Jews may pick olives from Palestinian groves
text: Prominent Israeli rabbi rules Jews may pick olives from Palestinian groves Israel’s prominent rabbi Dov Lior ruled on Friday that Jews may pick olives from Palestinian-owned groves in the occupied West Bank, Haaretz reported. Lior claimed the land belongs to the Jewish people, and said harvesting it publicly asserts Jewish ownership and fulfils the religious duty of "conquering the land." The ruling contradicts a letter issued a week earlier by six other Israeli rabbis , who said picking olives from Palestinian groves was forbidden as theft. It comes amid a surge in settler attacks during the olive harvest , with Israeli rights group Yesh Din recording at least 170 since 27 September. According to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, attacks during the olive harvest are particularly significant, as access to agricultural land and livelihoods are a major context for Israeli settler violence. It has documented injuries to farmers and the destruction of hundreds of olive trees across several towns in the occupied West Bank.

title: UK police assess Palestine Action post by security adviser’s wife
text: UK police assess Palestine Action post by security adviser’s wife British police said on Friday they were assessing a social media post after the wife of National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell appeared to express support for Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group which was banned as a "terrorist" organisation by the UK government in July 2025. Journalist and author Sarah Helm, who is married to Powell, responded on X to a post about the Irish novelist Sally Rooney, who this week announced her books would no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine Action. Helm said in the post: "God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action." In response, a Metropolitan Police spokesperson said the post was "being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required". Asked for comment, a government spokeswoman said: "These views are held by an individual who does not represent the government in any capacity." The Labour government’s proscription of the Palestine Action group means that expressing support for it or being a member is a criminal offence carrying a prison sentence of up to 14 years. text: Netanyahu calls for probe into ‘who initiated’ settler attack on Washington Post journalist Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said on Friday that the facts surrounding a settler attack on Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in the occupied West Bank “remain unclear”, and called for an investigation into “who initiated the violence”. In a statement on X, the Prime Minister’s Office said Levine had been “allegedly assaulted” during “the confrontation near Abu Falah”. It cited reports that some 200 “Arabs and far-left activists” had confronted around 40 “Israeli youths”, without saying where the figures came from. “We will not allow disputed incidents to be exploited to demonise the hundreds of thousands of law-abiding Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria,” the statement said, using the Israeli government’s term for the occupied West Bank. Witnesses said around 80 masked Israeli settlers attacked 64-year-old Levine, who was reporting on the Palestinian olive pickers in Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. title: Iran not seeking nuclear weapons and ‘ready for dialogue’, Pezeshkian says
text: Iran not seeking nuclear weapons and ‘ready for dialogue’, Pezeshkian says Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian denied on Friday that Tehran sought nuclear weapons as he expressed readiness for dialogue and condemned US sanctions. “Iran is not seeking nuclear weapons, and we consider the malicious propaganda against our country to be lies,” Pezeshkian said during talks with Georgia's prime minister Irakli Kobakhidze. “We have always been ready for dialogue. title: Spanish-built combat vehicles for Latvia to carry Israeli turrets despite arms embargo
text: Spanish-built combat vehicles for Latvia to carry Israeli turrets despite arms embargo A Spanish arms company has begun delivering infantry fighting vehicles fitted with Israeli weapons systems to Latvia, despite the Spanish government declaring an arms embargo on Israel last year, Israeli business daily Globes reported on Thursday. According to the report, Latvia ordered 84 of the vehicles last year from General Dynamics European Land Systems-Santa Barbara Sistemas (GDELS-SBS), which is headquartered in Madrid, in a deal worth around €800m ($929m), with all the vehicles due to be delivered by 2029. The infantry fighting vehicles, called Mednieks, are equipped with unmanned turret systems, called UT30 MK2, which are produced by the Israeli arms company Elbit Systems. “The delivery of infantry fighting vehicles is a significant step toward strengthening Latvia’s defence capabilities,” Latvia’s Defence Minister Raivis Melnis said last week, adding that the Mednieks would reinforce his country’s armed forces “as well as promote cooperation between the National Armed Forces and Nato allies”. title: Kohat Police Lines attack mastermind killed in joint operation in KP's Lakki Marwat: CTD
text: LAKKI MARWAT: The Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) said on Friday that its personnel had killed a terrorist commander in a joint operation with security forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Lakki Marwat on Friday. The CTD said in a statement that the slain terrorist, whom the law enforcement department identified as Zahid Gul, was the mastermind of the attack on Kohat Police Lines . In the attack on Sept 18, an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, following which terrorists stormed the compound and attacked police facilities. The attack resulted in the martyrdom of 17 policemen and six civilians. A total of eight terrorists were killed during the overnight clearance operation following the deadly two-pronged assault. The CTD statement said it conducted the joint operation in Lakki Marwat’s Walai Sagai area on Friday. “During the operation, a high-profile terrorist commander, Zahid Gul, who was affiliated with the khawariji Gul Bahadur group and the main mastermind behind the suicide attack on old Kohat Police Lines, was eliminated”, it added. According to CTD, the slain terrorist commander had led the explosive-laden vehicle to Kohat Police Lines on Sept 18. The statement said he was also wanted by security forces in connection with several other acts of terrorism. It added that he was also involved in a bank robbery in Balitang area of Kohat, in which Rs6 million was looted. The stolen money was subsequently distributed among terrorist factions

title: 'I am a normal human being': Khawaja Asif brushes off online trolling over AI-generated Marilyn Monroe riddle
text: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday brushed off online trolls who mocked him for responding to an AI-generated riddle featuring Hollywood icon Marilyn Monroe on the social media platform X. On Tuesday, the defence minister and PML-N stalwart replied to an AI-generated image of Monroe on X, which asked users to spot the one item that did not belong in the AI-generated image from the 50s. Asif reshared the post and pointed out that Monroe was wearing a smartwatch in the image. The original post shared by the defence minister has since been deleted. Subsequently, netizens questioned the propriety of the post, while Indian media also published articles on Asif’s online activities . On Friday, Asif was asked about the post and whether he operated his X account himself during an appearance on Geo News programme ‘ Naya Pakistan ’. “Two hundred per cent I operate it myself,” he said. “I have a personal life and a normal life. I am a normal human being; there is nothing special about me,” he emphasised, adding that he had “no pretences”. “They presented a riddle asking about what was amiss with this photo, something that should not have been present in 1956. And that was the smartwatch, so I wrote ‘watch’. What is non-serious about this?” Asif stressed that though he was the defence minister, he operated his own account “for fun” and asked: “Am I not Khawaja Asif? text: KARACHI: A sessions court in Karachi on Friday acquitted alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky in two narcotics cases. The first case was registered with the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in 2018 while the second case was registered at the Gizri police station in 2021. Anmol, who had been declared a proclaimed offender in both drug cases, had filed separate applications Section 265-K (power of Court to acquit accused at any stage) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for her acquittal. She appeared before the South additional and sessions judge via a video link at the hearing of her applications today, and the court acquitted her, citing a lack of evidence in both cases. The court ordered her release from jail if she was not required in any other case. Her brother, Nasir, has already been acquitted in the 2018 case. In August, a sessions court had acquitted Anmol in three narcotics cases registered at Karachi’s Gizri police station. Anmol’s arrest came to light in May when she appeared before a Karachi court. The arrest was made in connection with two cases, pertaining to the possession of drugs and an unlicensed weapon, registered at Karachi’s Garden police station. title: Short-term inflation surges to 11.38pc due to costly food
text: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.38 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 15, driven largely by higher food prices , according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday. Of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, prices of 23 commodities (45.10pc) increased, while those of seven items (13.72pc) declined, the data showed. Meanwhile, the prices of 21 items (41.18pc) remained unchanged from the previous week. Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum prices. The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly fell 0.04pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items. Unwilling to ease the petroleum levy, the government has continued to raise petrol and diesel prices on a daily basis. The surge in energy costs is not only fuelling inflationary pressures but also indirectly boosting sales tax collections through higher prices of goods and services. This is cost-push inflation, in which rising energy costs are followed by increases in food prices. As a result, households are under pressure from higher consumer prices. The statement described the development as a “historic milestone”, noting that Pakistan would return to the chairmanship for the first time since 1953. text: Eighteen countries, including Pakistan, on Friday strongly condemned the opening of the Colombian embassy in Jerusalem, stating that any move to recognise the city as Israel’s capital had no legal effect. text: Tesla CEO Elon Musk unveiled what he described as a “flying” car, equipped with thrusters, during a livestreamed event at his SpaceX rocket company’s facility on Thursday. Technical and regulatory challenges have so far prevented the much-hyped flying car sector from getting off the ground. Musk revealed his new Roadster sports car during a launch event at a SpaceX test facility in Texas. During the demo, which was livestreamed on Tesla’s X account, the car launched from a steep ramp and landed on its wheels. “Flying cars are real,” Musk said during the event. He added that the vehicle’s “success is not guaranteed” but that “it will probably work”. Musk said the car was equipped with “ultra high-pressure air tanks” to propel itself into the air. The tech billionaire described the development as “what happens when you have a collaboration with the world’s best car company and the world’s best rocket company,” referring to Tesla and SpaceX. The vehicle would go into production in 2028, he said. American aviation pioneer Glenn Curtiss debuted the first flying car prototype in 1917. But successful designs have become more seriously contemplated only in recent years as electric motors and high-performance batteries have advanced.

title: What does assuming the chairmanship of the IMF, World Bank governing boards mean for Pakistan?

The chairmanship carries mainly procedural and diplomatic responsibilities and does not give Pakistan additional authority over lending decisions by either institution. Pakistan last held the position in 1953, when the finance and economic affairs minister, Mohamad Ali, chaired the eighth annual meetings of the IMF and International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) in Washington. The bylaws of the IMF and World Bank set out the procedure for selecting a governor to chair their annual meetings. Section 6(a) of the World Bank’s bylaws states: “At each annual meeting the Board of Governors shall select a Governor to act as Chair”. text: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court on Friday fixed October 20 for the preliminary hearing of a petition filed by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and seeking to have the move declared unconstitutional. title: Diplomatic options

title: 'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu
text: 'In politics, I don't trust anybody': Trump says when asked about Netanyahu US President Donald Trump has said he does not trust anybody in politics when asked directly whether he trusts Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, weeks before Israel’s parliamentary election. In an interview with Newsmax’s “Finnerty” on Thursday, host Rob Finnerty asked whether he trusted Netanyahu. “I don’t trust anybody, honestly,” Trump replied. “I don’t trust anybody. In the world of politics, I don’t trust anybody,” Trump repeated. He did not say whether he had any particular concerns about Netanyahu, with whom he has kept a close political and military partnership. Asked whether he planned to get involved in the 27 October election, in which Netanyahu is seeking another term, Trump said: "Well, they'd like me to be. Yeah, they'd like me to be." He added: “I’ve had a very good relationship with him. We’ve had good success together.” Trump has previously held back from endorsing Netanyahu. In a Time interview published on 1 October, he said his “primary thing” was to help defend Israel.

The United States designated the group a "foreign terrorist organisation" in 2020. Khazali is the brother of the movement’s leader, Qais al-Khazali. Washington designated both brothers as "specially designated global terrorists", citing attacks including a 2007 assault that killed five US soldiers. The US Treasury also sanctioned them in 2019 over the killing of protesters in Iraq. Lawmakers on Thursday approved three deputy prime ministers and 11 ministers, completing Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The appointments include Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister. Zaidi's government has pledged economic reforms, anti-corruption measures and efforts to strengthen state institutions — but faces steep challenges, including rebuilding an economy battered by regional instability, tackling endemic corruption, and reining in Iran-allied armed groups, according to Reuters. title: Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue
text: Trump weighs new Iran strikes while insisting talks continue US President Donald Trump has said he is weighing fresh strikes on Iran without nuclear weapons or ground troops, while insisting negotiations with Tehran were under way. title: Textile exports rise
text: ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan’s textile and clothing exports rose 5.26 per cent to $5.026 billion in the first quarter of 2026-27 from $4.775bn in the same period last year. The marginal rise in export proceeds was attributed to elevated input costs, which eroded exporters’ competitiveness, and external shocks that disrupted shipments, according to data from the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics released on Thursday. Textile exporters have already warned the government that exports could slow further in the second quarter if no corrective measures are taken. Two major setbacks mainly contributed to slowing exports — suspension of trade with Afghanistan since October 2025 and falling exports to the Middle East due to the prevailing war in the region, especially the United Arab Emirates. PBS data showed readymade garment exports surged 15.69pc in value and 17.38pc in quantity during July-September FY27, while knitwear rose 4.14pc in value but fell 0.46pc in quantity. title: Persistence of force
text: WHILE the Balochistan insurgency has been simmering for many decades, in recent years, it seems to be spinning out of control. In July this year, Balochistan became the country’s most violent province, replacing KP for the first time. Some sources say there were 176 terrorist attacks, killing 438 people, including 127 security personnel, the highest ever in a month. This consistent increase in the insurgency’s lethality and spread implies a major mismatch between the threat and the measures taken to counter it. One major weakness is the imbalance between using armed force to address the challenge and subordinating the political dimension that sustains it. This begs the question: why do we continue to rely totally on the use of force to combat this insurgency, knowing that it has not worked for decades? Historically, COIN (counter-insurgency) strategies have succeeded only when they struck the right balance between armed force and political measures. At best, force can create the right conditions to end an insurgency, but only politics can use that opening to bring about peace through negotiations. In fact, David Galula, in his book Counterinsurgency Warfare: Theory and Practice, argues that a successful COIN strategy is “80 per cent political and 20pc military”. The owner has been arrested, while an inquiry is under way. These preliminary findings demand scrutiny. So do reports that concerns about the building’s condition had previously been raised. title: A chatbot to plug e-governance information gaps
text: LAHORE: Getting access to government services can prove costly, time-consuming and confusing. Though a myriad of services are provided through free government-run e-platforms, these remain fragmented across various domains, forcing people to run from pillar to post just to ascertain how they should go about availing a specific service. To solve this problem, a Karachi-based developer has come up with a simple yet elegant solution. The ‘Ask Pakistan’ platform, the brainchild of Raheel Siddiqui, is a website where a chatbot can help people seeking government services obtain the required information, thus bridging the gap between the state and its citizens. Talking to Dawn , Mr Siddiqui said that many non-tech-savvy people struggled with getting the required information.
